newsitem.title: USA: 3-yr note auction seen getting yields over 6.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: 3-yr note auction seen getting yields over 6.0 pct.

text.p: The U.S. Treasury's sale of $16 billion of three-year notes on Tuesday was expected to yield average rates above 6.0 percent, analysts said.
Yields on the current three-year were trading at 6.01 percent and yields on the when-issued three-year at 6.030 percent.

Carol Stone, economist at Nomura Securities International Inc, Friday's selloff should help all three of this week's offerings go well. In addition to the three-year issue on Tuesday, Treasury will offer $12 billion of 10-year notes on Wednesday and $10 billion of 30-year bonds on Thursday.
"The desk was fairly optimistic about all three issues this week after Friday's selloff," she said.

"With follow-through selling from Friday it seems we got rid of weaker hands at the tail," said Kevin Flanagan, money market economist and vice president at Dean Witter Reynolds Inc. Bonds fell sharply on Friday after a strong nonfarm jobless employment report and a firm manufacturing reading from the National Association of Purchasing Management.
It's a tough call since we've moved so much, but I still don't see much (price) movement," said Bill Retzenberger, a trader at Prudential Securities Inc.
Ratzenberger said all of the gains seen last week were erased by Friday's sharp dropoff.
